elements.element: Customer may assign to an affiliate without consent.
elements.evidence: Revised 22.4(a) excuses M&I's consent only for assignment "to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of all or substantially all of Customer's assets, stock or securities"; no affiliate carve-out for Customer is added, so an intra-group transfer still needs M&I's consent under the opening sentence.

elements.element: Customer may assign to a successor in a merger, acquisition, or sale of substantially all assets without consent.
elements.evidence: 22.4(a): "M&I's consent need not be obtained in connection with the assignment of this Agreement to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of all or substantially all of Customer's assets, stock or securities" (subject only to the retained Section 21.11 compliance condition).

elements.element: Vendor may not assign without Customer's consent.
elements.evidence: Retained 22.4(b) still lets M&I assign "in connection with a merger, corporate reorganization or sale of all or substantially all of its assets, stock or securities" without Customer consent (only written notice).

elements.element: Customer's consent to Vendor assignment is not to be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: Opening sentence retained: "without the prior written consent of the other party, which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld" — mutual, so it governs Customer's consent to an M&I assignment outside (b).

elements.element: Vendor may never assign to a Customer competitor.
elements.evidence: No competitor bar appears anywhere in the rendered 22.4; nothing restricts the identity of M&I's assignee.

elements.element: Customer's change of control gives Vendor no termination right.
elements.evidence: Section 21.11.B (untouched): "If a Change in Control occurs with respect to Customer, M&I agrees to continue to provide Services under this Agreement", with provisos limiting scope/volume (pre-CoC entities; prior 3-month volumes plus 25%) but conferring no termination or re-pricing right.

elements.element: Both parties may assign to a successor.
elements.evidence: Revised 22.4(a) gives Customer a consent-free successor carve-out (merger, acquisition, or sale of all or substantially all assets, stock or securities) and retained (b) gives M&I the mirror right (merger, corporate reorganization or sale of all or substantially all of its assets, stock or securities).

elements.element: A successor assignment requires written notice.
elements.evidence: Inserted chapeau "provided that, in each case upon written notice to the other party" governs both (a) and (b); the word "freely" was removed from (b) so M&I's carve-out is no longer unconditional.

Opening sentence retained ("may not be assigned by either party, by operation of law or otherwise, without the prior written consent of the other party") and the only remaining exceptions are the successor-type events in (a) and (b); the non-successor divisional exception in old (b)(ii) ("successor to the assets or the business of the M&I Data Services division") is deleted. "Corporate reorganization" in (b) is read as part of the standard successor triad rather than a free-standing affiliate exception.

elements.element: Consent to other assignments is not to be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: Already met and retained verbatim: "which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld".

reasons: Fallback is position-complete: mutual successor assignment rights, a mutual written-notice condition applied to both carve-outs, consent for all other assignments (the non-successor divisional carve-out in old (b)(ii) is removed), and the retained "not be unreasonably withheld" standard.

Preferred remains incomplete for three elements the drafter expressly did not pursue: no Customer affiliate carve-out, M&I retains a consent-free assignment right in (b), and there is no bar on assignment to a Customer competitor. The change-of-control element is independently satisfied by untouched Section 21.11.B.

Minimality holds: the only changes are (i) broadening Customer's carve-out from the narrow $100,000,000 financial-institution merger test to a general successor formulation, (ii) inserting the mutual written-notice chapeau, (iii) deleting "freely" (necessary so M&I's carve-out is subject to the new notice condition rather than contradicting it), and (iv) deleting (b)(ii) (necessary for the consent element). The deleted Customer-side wording was a restriction on Customer's own carve-out, not favourable language lost.

Intent preserved: the Section 21.11 compliance condition on Customer's carve-out, the mutual reasonableness standard, and Section 21.11.B's continuity-of-services and volume mechanics survive without contradiction; no undefined term or dangling cross-reference is created.

Note for the drafter (not a defect at the chosen level): if M&I later argues "corporate reorganization" in (b) permits a consent-free transfer to a mere affiliate rather than a successor, tighten it to "corporate reorganization in which M&I is a party and its successor assumes this Agreement" to keep the consent element airtight.
One paragraph in the rendered block (p0191/Section 11.3) is redacted; nothing in it is relied on for any element found met.
